observations.statement: Tree-drop behavior is cursor-hit-tested at drop time; copying in preserves symlinks, same-project drag defaults to copy, Shift selects copy-then-delete move, locked/read-only failures are surfaced without overwrite, overlong paths fail clearly, and keyboard and screen-reader alternatives are required.

Drop security requires an absolute normalized target under the project root and forbids any outside-project write; drag-out exposes only current-project paths. Large operations run off the UI thread with progress and cancellation, multi-item failures continue and end with a failure summary, successful targets refresh, and floating File Manager windows retain D&D capability.
Same-tree move/reorder and drop undo are optional for MVP, copy remains the safety default, while Settings is described as exposing both default-action and conflict-policy controls.

The MVP editor is the destination for File Manager and chat open-file actions. Its stated completion conditions cover tab activation, line/range navigation, save and dirty behavior, read-only visibility, large-file limits, transient states, explicit failure placeholders, editable empty files, canonical-path buffer uniqueness, and a five-second default highlight setting.

The editor strip expands when an open action targets a collapsed editor and persists collapse state per project. Docked and floating forms share tabs and buffers, exactly one floating editor window is supported, and tab close must prompt when dirty.

Save writes the authoritative path buffer; success clears dirty state, while failure preserves dirty and last-saved state and exposes a reason and recovery actions. GUI feedback represents dirty, conflict, read-only/degraded, change-marker, write-lock, stale/changed-on-disk, save/reload failure, and recovery attention as orthogonal facts.

Manual Revert is editor-owned disk reload, while Revert last agent edit is chat-owned through `cmd.chat.revert`; an omitted target resolves to the latest persisted-mutation assistant turn, the operation is whole-turn and potentially multi-file, and the backend refresh causes affected editor buffers to reload. Restore-point storage and manufacture remain backend-owned.

Unsaved recovery is required for local and remote-backed buffers. Recovered remote state is explicitly local-only, uses the exact unsynchronized banner, and cannot claim save or flush success until reconnect or destination revalidation; remote editing does not imply remote terminal or run/debug capability.

The live offline action copy is exactly `Work offline (cached files only)` and is available only for a validated cache or snapshot. Missing cache disables the action or shows a no-cache state, while reconnecting and disconnected states preserve buffers but block or explicitly queue round-trip operations and disclose unavailable or pending behavior for listings, searches/diffs, git, shell, LSP, and writes.

Chat line/range navigation is 1-based and inclusive, scrolls and highlights the target, clamps requests beyond EOF, and clears highlight on edit or cursor movement. Basic extension/shebang highlighting is the fallback, with LSP semantic highlighting permitted to augment or replace it.

MVP split groups have per-group tab lists and active tabs but share one path buffer and dirty state across views; cursor and scroll are per-view. The embedded document pane shares that buffer, dirty state, save history, restore points, and restore pipeline with File Editor.

DocumentPane `writing…` establishes a path-wide GUI write lock, renders the document read-only, requires an editor lock banner, permits streaming worker updates into the shared buffer, and releases when writing ends without creating a separate history branch.

Annotations anchor to canonical shared-buffer text and do not create a second buffer, dirty flag, or history branch; Send selection to chat creates thread-scoped composer preparation without mutating the file, and stale-render annotation mutation must fail instead of silently rebasing.

Dirty means in-memory content differs from last-saved content. Manual dirty-buffer reload requires Discard or Cancel, and changed-on-disk checks occur before Save and on editor or tab focus; dirty plus changed-on-disk uses one combined Reload, Overwrite, or Cancel prompt.

Editable text is UTF-8, line endings are preserved, writes occur only on explicit Save, binary and undecodable files are read-only with a reason, and read-only disk files block Save while allowing Save As. Files above 10,000 lines default to truncated read-only display, and a stated five-megabyte hard cap governs full-buffer loading.

Editor shortcuts are focus-routed across docked and floating windows. Per-project redb state specifies ordered tabs, one active index, per-path scroll/cursor state, a default 25 in-memory tab limit with LRU eviction, lazy restore with a default 50 persisted-tab limit, unsaved-exit prompting, crash recovery in both editor surfaces, named transient UI states, and keyboard/focus/screen-reader accessibility.

The project-scoped mention picker preserves canonical file identity, works in Assistant and Interview chat, and resolves an already-open file to existing editor state. File Manager, editor, and chat share project context and the File Manager file list.

FileManager canonically owns file-open and artifact-storage routing: scheme-bearing inputs use shared route semantics, opens bind to the active worktree, chat edit-card paths resolve from working directory plus relative path, artifacts are content-hash indexed, and GUI open-file visibility is filtered by execution role and approval scope.

Acceptance carry-through separates path-based `OpenFile` from identity-native `OpenArtifact`, assigns canonical route and OpenSubject contracts to Contracts_V0, preserves attempt-native runtime identity, normalizes legacy IDs before routing, and keeps detail, evidence, source, external-operation, and deep-link reference families distinct.

Broken paths or unreachable routes defer visibility rather than failing the run, create a navigable concern error, and provide a fallback route. Remote failures are classified into network-policy, unreachable, untrusted, permission-denied, and path-not-found states before recovery.

PM-native open-with targets are source editor, image viewer, workspace preview, detached preview, and diff review. Preview subjects retain source identity; HTML preview must disclose unavailable or degraded browser runtime instead of substituting screenshots, and browser/terminal runtime behavior remains owned outside FileManager.

Terminal and browser tab identities remain separate. FileManager owns breadcrumbs, outline, and Go to symbol; LSP uses documentSymbol or workspace/symbol, while unavailable-LSP behavior uses a labeled heuristic, regex, or indexed fallback.

candidate_findings.summary: Project-root containment is not operationally defined across preserved symlinks.
candidate_findings.obligation: A tree drop must never write outside the project root, while copying in must preserve a symlink rather than resolving it.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule gives only an example normalized-path prefix check and does not define normalization or the interaction between preserved symlinks and containment. Builders retain security-consequential discretion over what qualifies as `under the project root`.

candidate_findings.summary: Cancellation semantics for background copy-then-delete moves are missing.
candidate_findings.obligation: Large drops must be cancellable, same-project moves copy then delete, and multi-item failures continue with a final summary.
candidate_findings.gap: No state transition defines whether cancellation completes the current copy, deletes sources already copied, retains or rolls back destination items, classifies unstarted items, or reports canceled versus failed items. These choices materially change move safety and user-visible results.

candidate_findings.summary: Save As is simultaneously optional and apparently required for save failure.
candidate_findings.obligation: Save failure must keep the buffer dirty and expose actionable recovery with a reason.
candidate_findings.gap: One statement calls Save As optional, while the immediately following state contract says save failure leaves dirty state with retry, save-as, and reason. The acceptance surface cannot determine whether every save failure must expose Save As.

candidate_findings.summary: Buffer identity is not fully reconciled with worktree identity.
candidate_findings.obligation: The same file must have one canonical-path buffer, while files opened in different worktrees must have separate identity chains.
candidate_findings.gap: The buffer model names only file path as its key and does not state whether canonicalization happens after worktree binding or whether `execution_unit_context` participates in tab, buffer, recovery, and restore identity. Builders must choose the cross-worktree keying rule.

candidate_findings.summary: Write-lock acquisition can discard or conflict with existing user edits without a defined transition.
candidate_findings.obligation: When DocumentPane enters `writing…`, user edits must be locked across GUI surfaces while worker streaming continues in the shared buffer.
candidate_findings.gap: The File Editor may either prevent edits or immediately revert local edits, but the contract does not say what happens to a dirty buffer that already exists when the lock begins, how an in-flight edit is handled, or whether reverted input remains recoverable or undoable. The alternatives have materially different data-preservation behavior.

candidate_findings.summary: Turn-level backend revert has no dirty-user-buffer conflict contract.
candidate_findings.obligation: A chat-owned turn-level revert may affect multiple files, after which the backend emits refresh and the editor reloads affected buffers.
candidate_findings.gap: Manual disk Revert explicitly prompts before discarding dirty changes, but the backend refresh/reload path does not define what happens when an affected shared buffer contains unsaved user edits. There is no merge, prompt, preservation, rejection, or recovery rule for that overlap.

candidate_findings.summary: Remote cache validation, queued-write, and reconnect-conflict behavior are underspecified.
candidate_findings.obligation: Offline editing is limited to a validated cache or snapshot, remote save success requires reconnect or destination revalidation, and round-trip operations are blocked unless explicitly queued.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule does not define cache validation criteria, which writes may queue, queue ordering or durability, revalidation success evidence, or the decision path when the remote destination changed while offline. Builders can therefore claim materially different pending-write and synchronization outcomes.

candidate_findings.summary: Required unsaved recovery lacks a snapshot lifecycle and testable durability boundary.
candidate_findings.obligation: Local and remote-backed unsaved buffers must be recoverable after crash or quit-with-unsaved, with restore available from both editor surfaces.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule does not specify snapshot triggers or cadence, durability completion, retention, replacement, cleanup after successful save, selection among multiple snapshots, or the required behavior when the recovery store itself fails. Allowing `redb or temp` leaves consequential recovery guarantees to builders.

candidate_findings.summary: LRU eviction has no rule protecting dirty shared buffers.
candidate_findings.obligation: The GUI tab limit triggers LRU eviction, while dirty state is shared across views and unsaved content must be prompted for or recoverable.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule does not say whether a dirty buffer is evictable, whether eviction unloads only content or closes every group view, whether the user is prompted, or whether a recovery snapshot must complete first. The only explicit Save/Discard/Cancel trigger is quit or project switch.

candidate_findings.summary: The persistence schema does not represent the required split-group view model.
candidate_findings.obligation: Each MVP editor group has its own ordered tabs and active tab, and cursor/scroll state is per-view.
candidate_findings.gap: The defined redb shape provides one ordered tab list, one active index, and one scroll/cursor value per path. Split-group and active-group persistence is only a `Consider` item, so restart behavior may flatten groups, discard per-view positions, or choose an undocumented reconstruction.

candidate_findings.summary: The five-megabyte hard cap conflicts with the allowed settings range.
candidate_findings.obligation: The editor must never load more than 5 MB into one buffer, while users may configure the Hard cap setting.
candidate_findings.gap: The same line permits a Hard cap range of 2-10 MB without stating whether values above 5 MB override the absolute rule, are clamped, or are invalid. Either the `Never` rule or part of the GUI setting range becomes ineffective.

candidate_findings.summary: The required large-file system-editor affordance has no MVP handoff.
candidate_findings.obligation: Files above the hard cap must offer `Open in system editor` as an alternative.
candidate_findings.gap: The open-target contract says `system_default` is a future command and is not the MVP fallback. The capsule does not identify any other current command or capability that fulfills the required large-file action.

candidate_findings.summary: Scheme-bearing file inputs blur the OpenFile, OpenSubject, and OpenArtifact boundary.
candidate_findings.obligation: A scheme-bearing open input uses shared route semantics, `OpenFile` remains path-based for workspace files, and identity-native artifacts use `OpenArtifact`.
candidate_findings.gap: The capsule first describes a `file path` containing a route_target scheme, then restricts `OpenFile.path` to workspace paths, without defining the dispatch rule or rejection/normalization behavior that selects OpenSubject, OpenArtifact, or workspace realization.

candidate_findings.summary: Approval-scoped GUI visibility has no exact enforcement lifecycle.
candidate_findings.obligation: The GUI open-file list must be filtered by active execution role and approval scope, and restricted-scope files must not be shown to unprivileged users.
candidate_findings.gap: No predicate, authority source, scope-change event, already-open-tab behavior, direct-open response, or cache/persistence handling is defined. Builders retain consequential discretion over when restricted entries disappear and which surfaces the filter covers.

candidate_findings.summary: The mention picker has no mandatory minimum discovery capability.
candidate_findings.obligation: Invoking `@` must open a project-rooted picker that inserts identity-preserving mentions and reuses existing editor state.
candidate_findings.gap: All picker source categories are expressed as `may include`; the capsule does not require a baseline result source, matching behavior, ordering, deduplication, or no-results state. An implementation can satisfy the invocation contract while offering materially different file discovery.

candidate_findings.summary: Line/range validation is only specified for requests beyond EOF.
candidate_findings.obligation: Chat and editor navigation use 1-based inclusive lines and ranges and clamp a request beyond file length.
candidate_findings.gap: No result is specified for line zero, negative values, a reversed range, an empty range, or a range whose start is valid but whose end exceeds EOF. Builders must choose rejection, normalization, or clamping behavior.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: Drop targeting is explicitly the cursor-hit-tested folder or root row at drop time, not the selected row.
The security outcome is explicit: reject any drop target not under the project root and perform no write outside it; drag-out payloads contain only paths under the current project.
The floating-editor cardinality and replacement policy are explicit: one floating editor window, with a second drag re-docking the existing window and floating the newly dragged group.
Save-failure state preservation is explicit: dirty remains set, last-saved state does not advance, a reason is visible, and retry is present.
Recovered remote edits have exact live banner copy and cannot claim remote synchronization before reconnect and destination revalidation.
The single-buffer invariant across editor groups and Embedded Document Pane is explicit, including one authoritative dirty state, one persisted artifact, and one backend restore-point history.
Stale rendered selections have an explicit failure rule: mutating annotation creation fails and must not silently rebase to another span.
Changed-on-disk detection triggers and the combined dirty-conflict prompt are explicit, including Save and focus checks and Reload, Overwrite, or Cancel choices.
MVP writes are explicitly Save-only with no autosave; UTF-8, line-ending preservation, binary read-only behavior, and visible read-only reasons are stated.
OpenArtifact is explicitly artifact-ID-first and retains attempt-native run, node, thread, attempt, artifact, evidence, and cross-surface reference lineage before path realization.
Remote access failures have explicit user-visible category families separating network or trust failures, permission refusal, and missing paths.
HTML preview must explicitly disclose unavailable or degraded browser capability and must not substitute screenshots as a pseudo-browser.
Terminal and browser tab identities are explicitly distinct, and the ambiguous combined `/cap/browser-tab` concept is retired.
FileManager §10.2 is explicitly the Go to symbol owner, and stale §10.9 ownership references must be corrected rather than creating a new owner.

unknowns.statement: The exact route_target, OpenSubject, OpenArtifact, FileSafe, storage, and chat restore schemas cannot be established from this capsule.
unknowns.reason: The core delegates those contracts to named documents but does not include their definitions.

unknowns.statement: Whether same-tree reorder, drop undo, or configurable default Move is intended for the delivered MVP is unknown.
unknowns.reason: They are placed under Enhancements and individually marked optional or described as settings without an adoption decision.

unknowns.statement: The detailed browser and terminal launch, capability, permission, and runtime behavior cannot be reviewed in this assignment.
unknowns.reason: The core explicitly assigns runtime ownership to other specifications and owners.

unknowns.statement: Exact behavior for rename, delete, duplicate, compare, patch/conflict handling, watcher behavior, remote SSH/LSP, build/debug, session restore, refresh, and bulk operations is not supplied in this core.
unknowns.reason: The document itself labels these as sparse product seams rather than specifying their contracts in the assigned range.

unknowns.statement: Executable acceptance evidence for the listed editor and route/open conditions is not present in the capsule.
unknowns.reason: The core provides prose `Done when` conditions and acceptance carry-through rules but no test identifiers, receipts, or result records by which conformance can be verified.
